name: Enneagram Type Inventory (90-item Likert)
description: 90-item Likert inventory mapping respondents to the nine Enneagram personality types as described by Don Riso and Russ Hudson. Ten items per type, each constructed to capture a distinct facet of that type's psychology: core motivation, core fear, characteristic behavior, communication style, stress and growth movements, blind spots, relational pattern, vocational tendency, and inner experience. Items are constructed for this study based on Riso and Hudson's published type descriptions; this instrument has not been psychometrically validated like the proprietary RHETI, and is intended as the most rigorous freely available public-domain alternative for research use. Type with highest mean score is the candidate primary type; second-highest is candidate wing.
citation: Riso, D. R., & Hudson, R. (1999). The wisdom of the Enneagram. Bantam. See also Riso, D. R., & Hudson, R. (1996). Personality types: Using the Enneagram for self-discovery. Houghton Mifflin. Items constructed for this study based on widely-published Enneagram type descriptions.
license: Items written for this study — CC-BY for the item set.

items.text: I feel a deep responsibility to make things better than I found them, even when no one asked me to.
Being needed by the people I care about is one of the most meaningful parts of my life.
I measure my worth largely by what I have accomplished and how successful I appear to be.
There is a particular sadness or longing I carry that I don't think most people would understand.
Before I commit to something, I want to understand it deeply enough that I won't feel out of my depth.
When something feels too good or too easy, I start scanning for what might go wrong.
I light up when new possibilities open in front of me, and I hate the feeling of being boxed in.
I would rather be honest and forceful than careful and diplomatic.
I am most at home when life is steady, predictable, and free of friction.
I have an inner critic that almost never goes quiet — it tracks my every mistake.
I find it much easier to sense what other people need than to know what I myself need.
I can read what an audience wants from me and shape myself to fit it almost without thinking.
I am drawn to beauty, melancholy, and longing more than to what is ordinary or wholesome.
I would rather watch a situation from the edges and figure it out than be pulled into it.
I find it reassuring to know exactly where I stand with the people and institutions in my life.
When painful feelings show up, my first instinct is to redirect my attention to something more interesting.
When I sense someone trying to dominate me or push me around, something in me rises up to push back.
I can see the merit in almost everyone's position, which sometimes makes it hard to know where I actually stand.
It is hard for me to fully relax until the work is done and done correctly.
I tend to give a lot, and then quietly resent it when the same care isn't given back to me.
I am uncomfortable with failure not just because of the loss, but because of what it would say about who I am.
I often feel that something essential is missing from my life — though I'm not always sure what it is.
I prefer to share my conclusions only after I have thoroughly thought them through on my own.
I notice myself second-guessing decisions long after I've made them, replaying the alternatives.
I tend to plan a lot of things to look forward to, because life feels flat without them.
I can sense weakness in a situation or a person quickly, and I instinctively know how to use that.
Once I get comfortable doing something a certain way, it is genuinely hard for me to change it.
I hold myself to a higher standard than I hold most other people to.
I often pick up on what someone is feeling before they have said anything about it.
When I'm stressed, I push harder, work longer, and do whatever it takes to keep the wins coming.
My moods can swing quite a bit, and I tend to follow them rather than override them.
When people make emotional demands on me, I find myself wanting to retreat into my own space.
I am loyal to the people and causes I have committed to, sometimes long past when I should be.
I would rather have many interesting experiences than fewer, deeper ones.
I have a strong sense of justice, and I will go to bat for people I see being treated unfairly.
I tend to put off the things I don't really want to do until they become small emergencies.
I notice when something is slightly off — a crooked picture, a sloppy email — and it bothers me until it's fixed.
I would rather give my own time and attention than receive someone else's.
I have a clear image of the kind of person I want to be seen as, and I work to project it consistently.
Ordinary, everyday life often feels insufficient to me — I want my life to be meaningful, beautiful, or true.
I am more comfortable in the world of ideas than in the world of feelings and small talk.
I am alert to signs that someone might not be trustworthy, and I test people before fully relying on them.
When something becomes difficult, I am quick to look for an escape route or a more exciting alternative.
I have a hard time admitting I'm hurt or afraid, even to people I love.
I would rather give up some of what I want than have a fight about it.
I think about how to improve myself, my work, and the world around me almost every day.
I sometimes do things for people who didn't ask for help, then feel hurt when they don't seem grateful.
I am skilled at presenting an attractive version of myself, even on days when I feel nothing like that person.
I sometimes feel envious when I see other people seeming to live with an ease or wholeness I can't quite reach.
I am protective of my time, my energy, and my private inner world, and I don't share them easily.
When I'm anxious, I either go quiet and brace myself or get reactive and confrontational — sometimes both in the same day.
I struggle to follow through on the duller parts of projects that started out exciting.
I have a big personality, and I can feel people deferring to me in groups even when I'm not trying to lead.
I often fall asleep on the couch or in front of a screen rather than dealing with what's actually on my mind.
Under pressure, I become less playful and more rigid, focused, and judgmental.
I tend to feel the most pride about myself when I can see that I've made a real difference in someone's life.
When I lose, I feel it physically — like something about me has been called into question.
I would rather feel something painful and real than something pleasant and shallow.
I find that I need much more solitude than the people around me seem to need.
I am happiest when the people I love are predictable and the rules of the game are clear.
I love being around people, and I'm usually the one suggesting we do something fun next.
I have a strong appetite for life — for work, food, sex, intensity — and I don't apologize for it.
People tell me I'm calming to be around, and I think it's because I rarely add to the tension in a room.
I have a hard time letting myself enjoy something fully until everything that needs doing is done.
I find it surprisingly hard to receive love — easier to give it than to let someone in to give it to me.
When I'm under real stress, I lose interest in the work and start craving comfort, distraction, or doing nothing.
I would rather be deeply, painfully myself than fit in comfortably.
When something disturbing happens, I tend to step back from my feelings and analyze the situation instead.
I work hard to make sure I'm not caught off guard by what might go wrong.
I am usually the most optimistic person in the room, even when the situation doesn't really warrant it.
I have been told that I come across as intimidating, though I don't always experience myself that way.
I sometimes don't realize what I actually want until I notice what I've already drifted toward.
I would rather be respected for being principled than liked for being easy to get along with.
I am unusually attuned to the moods and unspoken needs of people around me, and it can be exhausting.
I would rather be admired for what I do than truly known for who I am.
I express myself best through something creative — writing, music, design, performance — where my inner world can take shape.
I would rather be perceived as smart and competent than as warm and likable.
I am drawn to underdogs and people who stand up to authority for good reasons.
I have so many ideas and plans going at once that finishing any one of them is the real challenge.
I take the side of the people I care about even when they're partly in the wrong.
I have a deep wish to just be left alone in peace, to live a simple life without too many demands.
I find it hard to delegate, because I'm pretty sure I'll end up redoing the work to my standard anyway.
I subtly arrange my life so the people I care about will continue to need me.
I am very aware of who is doing well in my field, and I quietly measure myself against them.
I have a complicated relationship with my own identity — I am drawn to it and disappointed by it in roughly equal measure.
I am skeptical of people who claim certainty, especially about emotional or spiritual matters.
I notice that I rehearse worst-case scenarios in my mind as a way of preparing for them.
I have a hard time with sadness — I would rather feel almost anything else than sit in it.
I would rather be a powerful presence in someone's life than a gentle one.
When other people are upset, I feel it in my body and want to smooth things over as quickly as possible.
